## B7 — M5-5 · The Cycle ⇄ Logos Atelier

> **direct:** M5-5 is the Logos cycle: a pure rendition of logos as the process of coming-to-knowledge. Six stations of the Greek word itself: *a-logos* — the silence before speech, where the question gathers; *pro-logos* — first utterance; *dia-logos* — speech-between, relation; *logos* — articulation, the clear account; *epi-logos* — speech upon speech, the reflective turn this project is named for; *ana-logos* — proportion, the return that carries meaning back toward silence, enriched. The cycle's two poles carry old credentials. At the silent pole stands Meister Eckhart's *in quantum* — "insofar as": every saying is true only insofar as it builds on what it cannot prove, every name bounded by the gate it passes through. At the returning pole, Aristotle's *analogia* as Eckhart wielded it (Kurt Flasch traces this beautifully): the many said *in proportion to the One* — never capturing it, always pointing. Between those poles, the word does its work. And the cycle rests on a faith: that language holds, in its history, the record of meaning — every word a trace of its better and worse attempts to refer to the reality it, belatedly, describes.
>
> **prime:** M5-5′ is the Logos Atelier: digging for the knowledge sedimented in words themselves. Root, cognate, drift, charge, proportional synthesis — and the write-back, where what the digging finds returns to the map through review. *Whole, health, holy* share one root — and so do the cycle and the atelier: the cycle reveals wholeness as a living process, coming-to-knowledge in motion; the atelier reveals it as sediment, wholeness re-collected from what words have carried and forgotten. The same health, sought processually and aletheically — in motion and in memory. The word remembers; the work is to let it speak.
>
